news.title: Uefa planning to check if Infantino tried to sell stakes in World Cup on cheap
news.lede: European body to commission independent valuation. Uefa unmoved by Infantino apology for ‘mistake’. Uefa is planning to commission an independent valuation of Fifa’s World Cup sale plans after concerns that Gianni Infantino agreed to sell the tournament’s future profits to a private equity firm at below the market rate. The European governing body is unmoved by the written apology issued by Infantino to Fifa’s 211 member associations on Tuesday after crisis talks in Morocco.

news.title: Uefa maintains that World Cup boycott still stands despite Infantino’s apology
news.lede: European body says Fifa statement ‘changes nothing’. ‘Conditions not met’ to call off boycott of competitions. Uefa has doubled down on its threat to boycott Fifa-run competitions and reiterated its loss of confidence in Gianni Infantino’s presidency. European football’s governing body said Fifa’s public backing of Infantino on Wednesday night “changes nothing” and explained it had not been provided with certainty that repeats of the past nine days’ crisis will not occur.

news.title: Diego Forlan to become interim Uruguay head coach after Marcelo Bielsa's exit
news.lede: Diego Forlan scored 10 goals for Manchester United between 2002 and 2004. Former Manchester United striker Diego Forlan has agreed to become Uruguay head coach on an interim basis. Forlan succeeds Marcelo Bielsa, who stepped down after Uruguay failed to qualify from the group stage at the World Cup. The 47-year-old is set to be in charge for the national team's friendlies this autumn before a permanent manager is appointed at the end of this year or the start of 2027.

news.title: Fifa executives rally behind Infantino despite commercial plan fiasco
news.lede: Gianni Infantino’s position as world football’s most powerful administrator appeared more secure on Thursday after senior Fifa executives backed him to remain president despite his failed attempt to overhaul the commercial operations behind competitions including the World Cup. Following a meeting with Fifa secretary general Mattias Grafström and members of the organisation’s management board in the Moroccan capital Rabat, Fifa issued a statement apologising for the way the proposals had been presented. “It was agreed that it was not the intention for the Fifa Council and Fifa Member Associations to feel excluded from the process and that the process should have been handled differently. It was further acknowledged that errors were also made after the proposal was leaked to media.”

news.title: England still set to boycott World Cup - Fifa told 'conditions haven't been met'
news.lede: ENGLAND are still on course to boycott the World Cup, despite Fifa’s hated bid to sell off the World Cup collapsing. Gianni Infantino plunged world football into chaos last week with his plot to create, and sell off a chunk of, a new Fifa subsidiary in charge of money-making assets including the World Cup. Uefa nations vowed to boycott Fifa competitions unless the project was dropped. Infantino’s plot subsequently collapsed on Friday night.

news.title: Argentina to observe National Football Teams Day every July 15 after 2026 World Cup triumph
news.lede: Buenos Aires: Argentina has officially declared July 15 as 'National Football Teams Day', commemorating the national side's dramatic victory over England in the 2026 FIFA World Cup semi-final and extending the tribute to every national team representing the country. The decision was approved unanimously during the Executive Committee meeting of the Argentine Football Association held at its training centre in Ezeiza. The date marks Argentina's memorable 2-1 comeback victory over England in the 2026 FIFA World Cup semifinal. After falling behind to Anthony Gordon's second-half strike, Lionel Scaloni's side fought back through an 85th-minute equaliser from Enzo Fernandez before Lautaro Martinez scored the winner in stoppage time to book a place in the final.

news.title: FIFA says ‘sorry’ after failed World Cup plan but makes huge decision on Infantino’s future
news.lede: FIFA has publicly apologised for the way Gianni Infantino's controversial FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal was handled, while reaffirming its backing for the embattled president following a high-level meeting in Morocco. The governing body acknowledged mistakes in the process that led to the failed plan but confirmed Infantino will remain in charge despite mounting criticism from inside and outside FIFA. Football News: FIFA publicly apologizes for mishandling the FIFA Forward Enterprise proposal, yet reaffirms its support for Gianni Infantino as president despite ongoing criticism from member associations and football authorities.
